one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings in the window: Q4 FY26 results usually come in early December, and FY27 guidance was already given at the 2026-09-30 Investor Day [2]. Events inside the window: (1) Cadence Q3 results, estimated 2026-10-26 (unconfirmed) [15]. These are the main read-across on EDA demand and AI-disruption sentiment (?). (2) Execution of the ~$1B buyback 'over the coming months' [2], about 1% of market cap. That is mild support. (3) Macro and AI-semis sentiment; Polymarket gives low recession odds [8]. Short-horizon regularities pull in opposite directions. Drift after a large guidance beat (FY27 EPS $19.08 vs ~$17.7-17.8 consensus [13]) argues up. Reversal risk argues down after a +33% move in 2.5 weeks ($367.70 close on 9/15 to $490.54 [14]), including a +12.8% gap day on 10/1. I treat these as roughly offsetting. So I centre the distribution at today's price (P(>=490.54)=0.50) with log-sigma ~13%, about annual vol / 3.5 (45%/3.5=12.9%). The sigma sits slightly above the usual monthly figure because volatility after an event is usually elevated.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, all looking 12 months out to FY28 numbers. FY28 EPS ~$22.9 (FY27 guide $19.08 grown 20%, a haircut to the mid-20s target) x 25x = $572 (50%). FY28 FCF ~$3.78B at a 3.6% equity FCF yield = $553 (25%). FY28 EBITDA ~$6.1B x 17x EV/EBITDA less ~$5B net debt = $521 (25%). Blended: ~$555.

bear.story: The AI-disruption narrative returns, e.g. another Kimi-style agentic or open-source EDA demo [5,7] or AI-native startups winning verification work. Add a China export-control flare-up and slow Amazon royalty ramp [11], and the multiple compresses to ~18x a trimmed FY28 EPS of ~$19-20. A macro or semis drawdown deepens the move.

base.story: Synopsys delivers its FY27 guide of $11.15B revenue and $19.08 EPS [2]. The market prices ~25x FY28 EPS of ~$22-23. Ansys synergies, the IP recovery (+11% in Q3 [3]) and buybacks support the case, and the stock holds its post-Investor Day re-rating.

bull.story: Agentic AI raises tool consumption and usage-based pricing takes hold, as Cadence's CEO argues [6] and newsletter writers echo [4]. IP royalties (Amazon) show up early and FY28 EPS of $24+ earns ~30x. This is roughly the HSBC $700 target and the Monte Investments $710 target [3,13].

thesis_break_reason: $340 is below the September 2026 low ($362.55 intraday / $367.70 close [14]). At that price the stock would be at ~18x FY27 EPS guidance, so the market would be pricing a cut to the guidance just given [2]. That would point to something fundamental: proprietary EDA losing share to AI or open-source flows, a renewed China export ban, or Ansys integration failing. Ordinary volatility alone is unlikely to explain it.

reasoning: Basic facts come from filings. Q3 FY26 revenue was $2.477B and non-GAAP EPS $3.91; FY26 guidance is $9.715B revenue and $15.07 EPS; net debt is ~$6.4B on 192.3M diluted shares [1]. At the 9/30 Investor Day the company guided FY27 to $11.15B revenue, $19.08 EPS, ~44% operating margin and ~$3.1B FCF, and set an FY30 margin target of ~50% [2]. That FY27 EPS guide is ~7% above consensus [13], which explains the jump from $415 to $490.54 [14]. My lane (alternative sources) adds context on the 2026 drawdown. The July Kimi K3 demo designed a 45nm chip in 48h with open-source tools and knocked ~8-9% off the stock [7]. Practitioners on SemiWiki largely dismissed it as a non-threat, though they named AI-native EDA startups as a real risk in verification [5]. Cadence's CEO argues that agents call more underlying tools, not fewer [6]. Two independent newsletters see an IP rebound and royalty upside [3,4]. One independent blog flags that the timing of Amazon royalties is undisclosed [11]. WARN notices show restructuring still under way, which supports margins [10]. Prediction markets put macro and geopolitical tail risk at low but non-trivial levels: US recession by end-2026 at 8.5% ($2.2M volume) and a Taiwan invasion by mid-2027 at 8.5% [8,9]. Fair value is ~$555, 13% above spot. For the 12-month ladder I blended a bear/base/bull mixture ($345/$555/$720 at 25/50/25%) with a lognormal centred on $525 at 40% vol. That vol is a little below the 45% realised figure, which was inflated by one-off shocks; the ±25-35% large-cap base rate is wider still for a name this volatile. Net result: P(>= spot) ~0.60 and median ~$530. The left tail stays fat because of the AI-disruption overhang. Research was limited: X/Twitter and Reddit block fetching (Reddit returned 403), so social sentiment comes only via forums and newsletters. Twelve Data estimates and statistics needed a higher plan tier.
